newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Endesa suspension stokes take-over talk.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Endesa suspension stokes take-over talk.

text.p: The decision by Spain's stock market watchdog to suspend trade in electricity companies Endesa, Fecsa and Sevillana stirred speculation of an impending take-over bid, analysts said.
Spain's National Stock Market Commission (CNMV) said on Friday it had suspended trade in the shares of the three companies pending a cabinet announcement later.
Analysts said the suspension had fuelled talk that Endesa may be on course to take a majority stake in Sevillana and Fecsa.
"The market is speculating that the cabinet will announce the approval of a take-over by Endesa," said one trader.
Endesa, which is 66-percent state-owned, already holds a 39.4 percent stake in Sevillana and a 49 percent stake in Fecsa.
"The only possibility is a takeoff," said a trader from Spanish broker Benito and Monjardin.
Traders were divided on the percentage Endesa might bid for in a possible take-over. An offer for Fecsa is likely to seek 100 percent control of the company's capital, many traders said.
An offer for Sevillana, however, is less clear-cut. Some traders said Endesa would attempt to acquire just 75 percent of the company, while others thought they would go for 100 percent.
The Industry Ministry told the CNMV that the cabinet would make the announcement after its weekly meeting on Friday.
Neither the Industry Ministry nor Endesa were available for comment.
Shares in Endesa traded at 7,950 pesetas at Thursday's close. Sevillana stood at 1,165 and Fecsa at 1,000 pesetas.
